description: One row per customer. It holds the customer's name and the behaviour signals the agent uses to judge which channel fits.
One row per card account: the attributes that rarely change. Balances and arrears move daily, so they sit in account_daily_snapshot.
One row per account per day: balance, arrears and the bank's risk view as they stood that day. The agent decides on the latest row and keeps the date it used, so a decision can be replayed.
One row per customer per channel. App push and letters need no consent row.
One row per restriction on file. Any active row stops all automated treatment for the customer, or for the one account when account_id is set.

One row per customer: when each guardrail area was last checked. No restriction rows can mean "checked, none" or "never checked"; only this table tells the two apart. Consent, contact history or restrictions older than 24 hours, or missing, make the agent fail closed (24 hours is a placeholder until compliance approves a limit).
One row per payment plan, deferral, settlement or promise to pay. The agent reads it before offering a new plan or deferral.

One row per outbound contact the customer received, from every system: the bank's dialler, letters, agencies and digital channels. The 7-contacts-in-7-days cap is about what the customer experienced, so every source counts.
One row per payment, including payments after charge-off. The agent works out each decision's outcome from these: the total of the posted payments inside the strategy's evaluation window.
One row per charged-off account in recovery. Recovery accounts are tracked by what remains of the charged-off balance, not by days past due.
One row per external collection agency on the bank's panel. Agencies are paid a share of what they recover, and are matched to accounts by product.
